plan: With no history and independent private values, the second-price auction’s weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value = 20, bidding 20 maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Ties resolve randomly; bidding exactly 20 is optimal on a 0.1 grid.

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and no exploitable history, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully. Bidding my value (29) ensures I win whenever the others’ top bid is below 29 and pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing nonnegative profit. Underbidding risks missing profitable wins; overbidding risks negative profit if I win when the price approaches or exceeds my value due to rivals’ bids. Therefore, I will bid my exact value.

Second-price sealed auction with independent private values. Dominant strategy is to bid your true value because you pay the second-highest bid; shading risks losing positive-profit wins, overbidding risks negative profit only if rules deviate. No learning available in this single round. With value = 45 on [0,49], this is strong; bidding 45 maximizes expected profit. Use exact value in 0.1 increments. Ties at 45 resolve randomly; acceptable given dominance of truth-telling.
